summary: 商业创新往往依靠小想法的累积、试错和协作。作者借企业家与公司的经历，分析灵感怎样在反复调整中变成可用的产品，以及企业为何寻求外部协助。
logic: 从失败和小改进中学习

sentences: Innovation describes the way that we develop new ideas, products and approaches, and it is one of the most vital human endeavours.
创新描述了我们发展新思想、新产品和新办法的方式，它是人类最重要的努力之一。
Over the history of humanity, innovation has made life better in so many different ways.
在人类历史上，创新以许多不同的方式改善了生活。
It is part of human nature to recognise the benefits of innovation; however, the majority of us have little comprehension of the processes that actually lead to innovation occurring.
承认创新的好处是人性的一部分；然而，我们大多数人对实际导致创新的进程缺乏了解。
It is a frequent topic for discussion in journals and university lecture theatres.
这是经常在杂志和大学讲座剧院讨论的一个专题。
However, in company boardrooms across New Zealand, the term is heard far too frequently and more caution should be applied.
然而，在新西兰各地的公司董事会中，这个词听得太多，应当更加谨慎。

Certainly, a recent international survey showed that the idea of innovation is so broad as to appear almost meaningless, with different sectors of the business world – or different divisions inside the same business – often defining innovation in their own way.
当然，最近的一项国际调查表明，创新的概念过于宽泛，几乎毫无意义，商业界的不同部门 — — 或同一企业内部的不同部门 — -- 往往以自己的方式定义创新。
paragraphs.gist: 创新改善了人类生活，但这个词在董事会上使用得太泛，国际调查也显示人们对它所指的活动缺乏一致认识。

paragraphs.brief: 旋盖如何改变饮料定位
sentences: While there is an obvious attraction to the new, innovation is not always about large-scale research and development projects or revolutionary business models; it can be on a small, highly localised scale and involve a step-by-step approach.
虽然对新的创新有明显的吸引力，但创新并不总是涉及大规模的研究和开发项目或革命性商业模式；创新可以采取小规模的高度本地化的做法，并涉及逐步的办法。
The famous case study of the drinks company Lucozade shows it can be as simple as adding a screw top to a bottle.
著名的饮料公司Lucozade的案例研究显示，它可以简单到在瓶子上添加螺丝顶。

This carefully managed change in packaging shifted the public perception of the product from a medicine to a sports drink and Lucozade profited handsomely, clearly showing their approach was successful.
包装方面的这种精心管理的变化将公众对产品的看法从一种药物转变为一种运动饮料，卢科萨德利润丰厚，这清楚地表明了他们的做法是成功的。
So what steps can businesses take to keep ahead in the innovation game?
那么，企业可以采取什么步骤来继续创新游戏？
paragraphs.gist: 创新可以只是局部小改进，葡萄适更换为旋盖包装后，公众便逐渐把它从药用饮品看成运动饮料。

paragraphs.brief: 电灯发明背后的长期投入
sentences: There seems to be a widespread belief that the world’s best ideas are sudden and intuitive.
人们似乎普遍认为，世界上最好的思想是突然的和直觉的。

Thomas Edison supposedly invented the light bulb with a sudden moment of clarity, but in fact the book Edison: His Life and Inventions shows that Edison’s own inspiration usually resulted from laborious experimentation, rather than a moment of genius.
托马斯·爱迪生的发明灯泡突然清晰的瞬间，但事实上，《爱迪生：他的生命与发明》的书显示爱迪生自己的灵感通常来自艰苦的实验，而不是天才的瞬间。
Thus, business managers are at risk of overestimating the pace of development while underestimating the amount of perseverance needed.
因此，业务经理有可能高估发展速度，同时低估所需的毅力。
This is why we must reject the false assumption that innovation is just a moment of brilliance waiting to strike.
因此不能想当然地把创新视作某个总会突然降临的灵感时刻。
paragraphs.gist: 爱迪生发明电灯并非传说中那样灵光一现，若管理者低估反复试验所需的投入、又高估进展速度，便会误判创新过程。

sentences: No exploration of innovation is complete without mention of Steve Jobs, the late chief executive officer (CEO) of Apple.
没有提及苹果公司已故首席执行官史蒂夫·乔布斯，任何创新探索都是不完整的。
No-one encapsulated the creative essence of Silicon Valley, the home of many global tech companies, better than Jobs, but he has also been accused of arrogance.
没有人概括了硅谷这个全球技术公司所在地的创造性本质，比乔布斯要好，但他也被指控为傲慢。
Jobs’ managerial approach often irritated his co-workers but, in part, it was the fuel for his visionary innovations.
工作管理方式往往刺激他的同僚，但部分地，这是他富有远见的创新的动力。
He felt it his duty to make society a better place, but his egotistical behaviour could have undesirable consequences, too.
他认为他有责任让社会更美好，但他的自大行为也可能产生不良后果。
Jobs’ former employees have suggested this type of demanding behaviour affects sickness rates and group morale, which in turn may squash creativity and innovation.
乔布斯的前员工认为，这样严苛的作风会影响员工生病率和团队士气，进而可能扼制创造力与创新。
paragraphs.gist: 乔布斯苛求细节的作风为其远见注入动力，但也令同事不满、影响士气和健康，企业模仿明星领袖时须看见这种代价。

paragraphs.brief: 试错对于渐进创新的价值
sentences: In his 2011 TED (Technology, Entertainment, Design) Talk, economist Tim Harford made this statement: ‘Show me a successful complex system, and I will show you a system that has evolved through trial and error.’
经济学家蒂姆·哈福德在2011年TED(技术、娱乐、设计)演讲中说道：“ 给我讲讲一个成功的复杂系统，我将向你们展示一个通过试验和错误演变的系统。”
It sounds like common sense, and some commentators have claimed Harford’s TED Talk was not persuasive, because it was stating the obvious.
这听起来像常识，有些评论家说Harford的TED演讲没有说服力，因为它是说清楚的。
But he responds that a trial and error approach is not all that obvious, because society expects all problems to have a quick and simple solution.
但是他回答说，试探和错误的方法并不十分明显，因为社会期望所有问题都能有一个迅速和简单的解决办法。
Harford is right to point out that both consumers and investors expect consistent and clear breakthroughs.
Harford正确地指出，消费者和投资者都期望取得一致和明确的突破。
But the value of step-by-step innovation is often underrated and failure may in fact be crucial to eventual success.
但是，逐步创新的价值往往被低估，失败实际上可能对于最终成功至关重要。
paragraphs.gist: 哈福德主张复杂系统通过试错才逐步成功，消费者和投资者虽期待清晰而连续的突破，小步改进甚至失败也可能成为成功的条件。

paragraphs.brief: 印刷术带来的跨行业连锁反应
sentences: Former chief solutions officer at Yahoo, Tim Sanders, believes that innovation is only ‘little ideas that combine with other little ideas that improve themselves into game-changing ideas’.
雅虎前首席解决方案官蒂姆·桑德斯认为，创新不过是“一些小点子与另一些小点子结合，在不断改进中变成改变局面的想法”。
This snowballing effect has similarities to the phenomenon that author and broadcaster Steven Johnson calls the ‘hummingbird effect’ of innovation.
这种雪球效应与作家和播音员Steven Johnson称创新的“蜂鸟效应”相似。
This points out that progress in one area or discipline can end up triggering small but significant developments elsewhere entirely.
这表明，在一个领域或纪律方面取得的进展最终可能完全引发其他地方的微小但重大的事态发展。
A good case to cite in support of this universal truth would be Gutenberg’s printing press, which was revolutionary in itself for making books accessible to the masses.
古滕贝格的印刷厂是支持这一普世真理的一个很好的例子，它本身就具有革命性，使大众能够阅读书籍。
However, the press also affected an unrelated industry by causing a rise in demand for reading glasses.
然而，新闻界也影响到一个无关的行业，造成对阅读眼镜的需求增加。
This highlights the wider idea of connectivity, which is an essential component of innovation.
这突出了更广泛的连接概念，这是创新的重要组成部分。
paragraphs.gist: 古腾堡印刷术不仅变革图书业，还推高了阅读眼镜的需求，说明创新往往由小点子叠加，并在原本无关的行业引起连锁变化。

paragraphs.brief: 纳米技术企业为何选择合作
sentences: When Kode Biotech won a recent innovation award, CEO Steve Henry had this to say: ‘Most people think innovation is invention, but they don’t understand that innovation is the conversion of invention into something useful.’
科德生物科技公司最近获得一项创新奖后，首席执行官史蒂夫·亨利说：“大多数人以为创新就是发明，却不明白创新是把发明转化为有用的东西。”
This is particularly true when it comes to Kode’s highly specialised use of nano-technology.
科德对纳米技术的高度专业化使用尤其如此。
Henry says that Kode cannot chase all the opportunities it has created.
亨利说科德不能追逐它创造的机会
Instead, Kode’s approach is to collaborate with similar nano-technology businesses, which take its innovations and develop them into commodities that can be sold in the marketplace.
相反，Kode的办法是与类似的纳米技术企业合作，这些企业将创新发展成为可以在市场上销售的商品。
paragraphs.gist: 科德生物科技无法独自追逐纳米技术带来的每种机会，便与同行合作开发应用，把发明变成真正有用的产品。

paragraphs.brief: 外聘团队突破大企业创新障碍
sentences: Innovation can be hectic and disorganised, but that is the way that radical new ideas sometimes come about.
创新可能是杂乱无章的，但激进的新思想有时就是这样产生的。
But, for established businesses, the disorderly nature of innovation can seem discouraging.
但是，对于已确立的企业来说，创新的无序性质似乎令人沮丧。
Previously Unavailable, a specialist innovation consultancy, says that while 84% of businesses consider innovation critical to their future, only 6% are satisfied with their innovation efforts.
一位专家创新顾问曾指出，尽管84%的企业认为创新对其未来至关重要，但只有6%的企业对其创新努力感到满意。
Previously Unavailable uses a process called Black Box, which was developed following a study at Harvard Business School.
此前没有机会使用一个称为黑盒的过程，这是在哈佛商学院研究后开发的。
Black Box was formed to overcome the barriers that prevent innovation in larger organisations.
成立黑盒是为了克服妨碍较大组织创新的障碍。

Using this unique system, Previously Unavailable will lease a team of innovation experts on a short-term basis to client organisations to assist with conceiving, developing and launching new products and business innovation.
利用这一独特的系统，以前没有的将短期向客户组织租赁一个创新专家团队，以协助构思、开发和推出新产品和商业创新。
It seems probable that this sort of innovation consultancy will become increasingly common, just as businesses already employ specialist consultants for legal, financial or marketing services.
似乎这种创新咨询会越来越普遍，正如企业已经为法律、金融或营销服务聘用专家顾问一样。
paragraphs.gist: 多数企业重视创新，却很少满意自身成果，咨询公司因而推出短期派驻专家的“黑箱”服务，帮助成熟企业克服内部障碍。

items.en: Most people naturally understand how innovation happens.
items.zh: 大多数人自然地理解创新是如何发生的。
items.why: 题干说“most people naturally understand”, 意思是“多数人本来就懂"。原文却明确说“多数人几乎不了解” 创新发生的过程，是直接相反的观点，因此答案为 NO。

items.en: The word ‘innovation’ is overused in business in New Zealand.
items.zh: `创新 ' 一词在新西兰的商业中被过度使用。
items.why: “heard far too frequently”= 出现得太频繁、用得太多，对应题干的“overused (过度使用)”。地点也正是“公司董事会议室 across New Zealand”,与题干完全一致，所以是 YES.

items.en: There are many interpretations of what innovation means in business, according to one global study.
items.zh: 根据一项全球研究，对创新在商业中的含义有许多解释。
items.why: “recent international survey”就是“一项全球性的研究/调查”。结果是不同部门“各自给出自己的定义”,说明对“创新”有很多不同解释。与 iF “many interpretations of what innovation means in business” —3X, litt YES。

items.en: Research and development projects have a higher priority today than in the past.
items.zh: 研究和发展项目今天比过去更优先。
items.why: 作者指出，重大研发和小规模改进都可以构成创新，讨论的是创新的规模。文中没有比较研发项目在今天和过去的优先级。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: What is the writer doing in the third paragraph?
correct: dismissing one common idea about innovation
反驳一种关于创新的常见看法。

items.en: What is the writer’s main point in the fourth paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第四段的要点是什么？
correct: There are pros and cons to strong leaders.
强势的领导者既有优势，也可能带来问题。

items.en: The writer refers to Gutenberg’s printing press in order to
items.zh: 作者提到古滕贝格的印刷机，以便
correct: give an example of a general rule about innovation.
举个例子来说明创新的一般规则。

items.en: What is the writer’s main point in the seventh paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第七段的要点是什么？
correct: Companies should cooperate to turn ideas into products.
公司应进行合作，将想法转化为产品。

items.en: According to the writer, companies like Previously Unavailable
items.zh: 按作者的说法，像 Previously Unavailable 这样的公司能提供什么服务？
correct: can be hired to give businesses advice about innovation.
可以被雇用向企业提供关于创新的建议。

items.en: A book about the life and work of Thomas Edison suggests that
items.zh: 一本关于托马斯·爱迪生生活和工作的书表明
items.answer: E · innovation requires a great deal of hard work.
items.solution: 创新需要大量艰苦的工作。

items.en: People who have worked for CEOs like Steve Jobs claim that
items.zh: 曾在史蒂夫·乔布斯这类首席执行官手下工作的人指出，
items.answer: G · certain personality types can limit innovation.
items.solution: 某些个性可以限制创新。

items.en: Critics of Tim Harford’s 2011 TED Talk say that
items.zh: 批评Tim Harford2011年TED演讲的人说
items.answer: C · expressing what everyone already knows is pointless.
items.solution: 表达大家已经知道的东西是毫无意义的。

items.zh: 史蒂文·约翰逊提出的“蜂鸟效应”表明，
items.answer: B · innovation may influence a completely different field.
items.solution: 创新可能会影响一个完全不同的领域。

items.en: Kode Biotech CEO Steve Henry believes that
items.zh: 科德生物科技CEO 史蒂夫亨利相信
items.answer: D · innovation can be enhanced through collaboration with similar companies.
items.solution: 创新可以通过与类似公司的合作得到加强。

pairs: 使用过度／听得过于频繁
innovation requires a great deal of hard work
创新需要艰苦的实验和工作
innovation can be enhanced through collaboration with similar companies
通过与同类企业合作创新
points: 题干说“most people naturally understand”, 意思是“多数人本来就懂"。原文却明确说“多数人几乎不了解” 创新发生的过程，是直接相反的观点，因此答案为 NO。
题干问“科德生物科技CEO 史蒂夫亨利相信”。定位句写到“相反，Kode的办法是与类似的纳米技术企业合作，这些企业将创新发展成为可以在市场上销售的商品”。
clauses: Innovation describes the way …, and it is one of the most vital human endeavours.
“that we develop new ideas, products and approaches”修饰前面的 way。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 way，再把修饰信息接回主句。
… is not always about large-scale research and development projects or revolutionary business models; it can be on a small, highly localised scale and involve a step-by-step approach.
连接词 while 引出“While there is an obvious attraction to the new, innovation”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
